topic: Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth as CEO and Announces More Than $1 Billion in Planned Growth Investments

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth as CEO and Announces More Than $1 Billion in Planned Growth Investments

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Equinox has appointed Brendan Whitworth CEO as the company enters its next phase of growth. Whitworth was most recently CEO of Anheuser-Busch, where he led all aspects of long-term strategy and growth. He will also serve as a director on the Equinox board. Harvey Spevak, who has led Equinox since 1999, will serve as chairman. Whitworth said member loyalty will be central to his approach. “People embrace Equinox in their daily lives and routines because of how it makes them feel and what it helps them achieve, and I take seriously the responsibility of upholding that standard of excellence and earning our members’ loyalty day in and day out,” he said. Spevak said he was personally involved in bringing Whitworth to the company and has known him for several years. “Brendan has a deep appreciation for what Equinox represents and a deep understanding of what makes exceptional brands resonate with consumers,” said Spevak. The leadership change comes as Equinox reports strong demand across its portfolio. The company operates 118 clubs in 18 major markets and says recent club openings have far surpassed projections. It cites double-digit topline growth, with membership numbers, activity and check-ins at all-time highs.

en.headline: Equinox Names Brendan Whitworth as CEO and Announces More Than $1 Billion in Planned Growth Investments

topic: OneSpaWorld Posts Record Q3 Revenue as Cruise Wellness Business Surges

facts.label: Story
facts.value: OneSpaWorld Posts Record Q3 Revenue as Cruise Wellness Business Surges

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The operator reported its 22nd consecutive quarter of record growth as demand grows for fitness and wellness travel experiences OneSpaWorld continues to ride a wave of demand for health and wellness experiences at sea. The operator of spas, fitness and wellness centers aboard cruise ships and at destination resorts reported record third-quarter revenue of $276.5 million, up 7% year over year, marking its 22nd consecutive quarter of record year-over-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth. Net income climbed 16% to a record $28.2 million, while adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $39.2 million, also a quarterly record. The strong performance prompted OneSpaWorld to raise its full-year financial outlook, with the company now expecting revenue between $1.033 billion and $1.038 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $138 million to $140 million. “We delivered excellent third quarter performance, reporting results that surpassed our guidance and marking our 22nd consecutive record quarter of year-over-year growth in Total revenues and Adjusted EBITDA,” said Leonard Fluxman, the executive chairman and CEO of OneSpaWorld. “Our sustained momentum reflects the durability of our business model, the successful execution of our strategy and our unwavering commitment to deliver memorable experiences for guests of our health and wellness centers at sea and on land,” Fluxman added.

en.headline: OneSpaWorld Posts Record Q3 Revenue as Cruise Wellness Business Surges

facts.value: In 1983, Mark Mastrov founded 24 Hour Fitness. Forty years and more than 60 countries later, he’s building a 45,000-square-foot facility in his home town with everything a fitness enthusiast needs and wants. 24 Hour Fitness announced Founders Club by 24 Hour Fitness, a new club designed by Mastrov that opens in Summerlin in early 2027. “I’ve spent my career building thousands of gyms in more than 60 countries,”said Mastrov. “This location and facility in Las Vegas is something special. Every detail reflects what I’ve learned about what members are actually looking for today. Summerlin is one of the fastest-growing communities in the country, which makes it the right place to show what the next generation of fitness looks like.” Founders Club is built around what Mastrov believes matter most: the right equipment, and plenty of it; a big open well lit space, at more than 45,000 square feet; classrooms and a recovery room to support well rounded training, and a variety of amenities that make the gym special. It’s designed for people who want to get after it, where they can train, recover and stay a while. The club represents a $10 million investment, including more than $1 million in recovery equipment alone. Located at 9200 West Sahara Avenue, the brand new club will include: 25,000 square feet of free weights and strength training, including 12 platforms.
